newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania promises not to storm rebel towns-Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albania promises not to storm rebel towns-Italy.

text.p: Albania's president Sali Berisha has assured Italy that military forces will not seek to retake southern towns held by armed rebels through use of force, Italy said on Thursday.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told reporters Berisha had given assurances that the army would try to isolate the towns and then try to reach a settlement for rebels to lay down their arms.

"We have urged the Albanian authorities to refrain from using force to put an end to the revolt in the southern cities. We have been assured by President Berisha...that they will do so and that their purpose is of course to try to re-establish law and order in the entire country," Dini said.
"We are being assured that they will not go beyond the surrounding, the isolating of the areas that are now out of the control of the government," Dini added.
Dini spoke after talks with Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo in Rome on an urgent mission he will make to Tirana on Friday following a declaration of a state of emergency there.
Van Mierlo, whose country holds the European Union presidency, said he would urge Berisha and the opposition to form a government of national reconciliation as a way of putting an end to the crisis.
